FUNDING REPORT 
Between July 2025 and June 2026, the Leduc Center for Civic Engagement submitted 
17 grant /gift requests totaling $534,435. Of these, 10 grants were awarded, bringing in 
$354,435 to support our programs and initiatives. 
Key Funding Highlights: 
•   BayCoast Bank committed $75,000 over three years to support our 7th Grade College 
Positive Campus Tours and the 8th Grade College and Career Awareness Youth 
Summit. We are currently in the second year of this funding. 
•   The Carney Leaders Program received $98,000 to continue developing a pipeline of 
civic-minded student leaders. 
•   State Representative Christopher Hendricks secured $75,000 in funding for our 
America Reads literacy program. 
•   The Massachusetts Department of Higher Education awarded a $14,920 Hunger-Free 
Campus Initiative grant to support the work of Jeanne's Cupboard Food Pantry. 
•   The Leduc Center was awarded an AmeriCorps VISTA member, valued at $81,515, to 
expand mentoring initiatives that support student success and retention. 
•   A $50,000 proposal submitted to the Robert F. Stoico/FIRSTFED Charitable 
Foundation is pending and would expand the Claire T. Carney Leaders Program. 
The continued support of our funding partners— is essential to sustaining and 
expanding the Leduc Center's mission of empowering students through civic 
engagement, leadership development, service, and community partnerships.
